extracted.intended_audience: GAP users and developers working with tables of marks and character tables (computational group theorists)
extracted.subtask_description: Reference-manual guidance for producing and manipulating tables of marks and character tables in GAP, including function preconditions, behaviours, options, and conventions for interfacing these tables with groups.

rubrics_metrics.name: RepresentativeTom and variants
rubrics_metrics.description: RepresentativeTom(tom, sub) returns a representative of the sub-th conjugacy class of subgroups of tom when tom is a table of marks with IsTableOfMarksWithGens value true. RepresentativeTomByGenerators(tom, sub, gens) and RepresentativeTomByGeneratorsNC(tom, sub, gens) return a representative of the sub-th conjugacy class of subgroups of tom as a subgroup of the group generated by gens (i.e., replacing standard generators by gens).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the attribute StraightLineProgramsTom is set in tom then methods for RepresentativeTomByGenerators and RepresentativeTomByGeneratorsNC are available. RepresentativeTomByGenerators checks whether mapping generators of tom to gens extends to a group isomorphism and returns fail if not (mainly intended for debugging). RepresentativeTomByGeneratorsNC omits all checks, to avoid overhead when gens are known to be standard generators; using NC requires StraightLineProgramsTom. Example: gap> RepresentativeTom( a5, 4 ); Group([ (2,3)(4,5), (2,4)(3,5) ]).

rubrics_metrics.name: FusionCharTableTom behaviour and cases
rubrics_metrics.description: FusionCharTableTom(tbl, tom) determines the fusion of classes of elements from an ordinary character table tbl to the classes of cyclic subgroups on tom, returning a list where position i gives the position of the class of cyclic subgroups in tom generated by elements in the i-th conjugacy class of tbl.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Three cases are handled: (1) fusion explicitly stored on tbl (then nothing to do, happens when both tbl and tom are library tables); (2) UnderlyingGroup values of tbl and tom are known and equal (then the group is used to compute fusion); (3) neither fusion nor group info available (only necessary conditions can be checked; if insufficient to determine fusion uniquely then FusionCharTableTom returns fail). Use PossibleFusionsCharTableTom(tbl,tom[,options]) to compute the list of possible fusions consistent with checked criteria. Options include 'fusionmap' (a parametrized map approximating desired map) and 'quick' (Boolean: return immediately once one possibility remains; default false). Example: gap> fus:= FusionCharTableTom( a5c, a5 ); [ 1, 2, 3, 5, 5 ].

rubrics_metrics.name: PossibleFusionsCharTableTom semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: PossibleFusionsCharTableTom(tbl, tom[, options]) computes the list of possible fusions from tbl to tom according to the criteria that have been checked.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If FusionCharTableTom returns a unique fusion then the list returned here contains exactly that fusion; if FusionCharTableTom returns fail then the length of the list is different from 1. The optional options record may contain 'fusionmap' and 'quick' as described under FusionCharTableTom.

rubrics_metrics.name: PermCharsTom behaviour (via fusion or table)
rubrics_metrics.description: PermCharsTom(fus, tom) or PermCharsTom(tbl, tom) returns the list of transitive permutation characters from the table of marks tom.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In the first form, fus must be the fusion map from the ordinary character table of the group of tom to tom (as from FusionCharTableTom). In the second form, tbl must be the character table of the group of which tom is the table of marks. If the fusion map is not uniquely determined then fail is returned. When fus is given, each transitive permutation character is represented by its values list; when tbl is given, permutation characters are class function objects. Examples show lists and Character( CharacterTable( "A5" ), [...] ) representations; PermCharsTom( fus, a5 )[1] yields [60,0,0,0,0].

rubrics_metrics.name: TableOfMarksCyclic construction rule
rubrics_metrics.description: TableOfMarksCyclic(n) returns the table of marks of the cyclic group of order n.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A cyclic group of order n has, for each divisor d of n, a cyclic subgroup of order d. Example: Display( TableOfMarksCyclic( 6 ) ).

rubrics_metrics.name: TableOfMarksDihedral construction rule
rubrics_metrics.description: TableOfMarksDihedral(n) returns the table of marks of the dihedral group of order m (with m = 2n).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For each divisor d of m the dihedral group contains subgroups of order d according to: if d is odd and divides n then only one cyclic subgroup of order d; if d is even and divides n then there is a cyclic subgroup of order d and two classes of dihedral subgroups of order d (which are cyclic in the case d = 2); otherwise (d does not divide n) there is just one class of dihedral subgroups of order d. Example: Display( TableOfMarksDihedral( 12 ) ).

rubrics_metrics.name: TableOfMarksFrobenius construction rule
rubrics_metrics.description: TableOfMarksFrobenius(p, q) computes the table of marks of a Frobenius group of order p*q, where p is a prime and q divides p − 1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires p prime and q | (p - 1). Example: Display( TableOfMarksFrobenius( 5, 4 ) ).

rubrics_metrics.name: TomLib library access for tables of marks
rubrics_metrics.description: The TomLib package provides access to several hundred tables of marks of almost simple groups and their maximal subgroups; if installed, tables can be fetched via TableOfMarks with a string argument.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the GAP Character Table Library is also installed and contains the ordinary character table for the group, TableOfMarks can be called with that character table. All library names are available via AllLibTomNames. Example: names:= AllLibTomNames();; "A5" in names; true.

rubrics_metrics.name: Five ways to obtain a character table
rubrics_metrics.description: Character tables in GAP can be obtained by: (1) computing the table from a group; (2) reading a file containing the table data; (3) constructing the table using generic formulae; (4) deriving it from known character tables; (5) combining partial information about conjugacy classes, power maps, and character tables of subgroups/supergroups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CharacterTable (71.3.1) supports (1)-(3). Methods and algorithms for computing irreducible characters (case 1) are described in 71.14. Generic tables are in CTblLib: Generic Character Tables. Some derivations (case 4) are discussed in 71.20. The last possibility (5) is not yet supported in GAP.

rubrics_metrics.name: CharacterTable operation behaviour and lazy Irr computation
rubrics_metrics.description: CharacterTable(G[,p]), CharacterTable(ordtbl,p), and CharacterTable(name[,param]) behave differently: with a group G it calls OrdinaryCharacterTable; with group/table and prime p it calls BrauerTable; with a name string it fetches from the CTblLib library (error if library not loaded).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Irreducible characters (Irr) are not computed by CharacterTable upon construction unless read from the library; Irr is computed lazily when first accessed (e.g., Display triggers computation). This design lets CharacterTable return quickly when only 'table head' information is needed (class lengths, power maps, etc.). The HasIrr filter indicates whether irreducibles have been computed.

rubrics_metrics.name: BrauerTable computability criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: BrauerTable(ordtbl,p) or BrauerTable(G,p) returns the p-modular Brauer character table if GAP can compute it; otherwise it returns fail.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The p-modular table can be computed when: (•) the group is p-solvable (Fong–Swan Theorem); (•) the Sylow p-subgroup of G is cyclic and all p-modular Brauer characters of G lift to ordinary characters (detectable from the ordinary table); (•) ordtbl stores information how it was constructed from other tables and the Brauer tables of source tables can be computed; (•) ordtbl is a library table that contains the p-modular table. The default method delegates to BrauerTable for the ordinary character table; ComputedBrauerTables stores computed Brauer tables at position p; new methods should be installed for BrauerTableOp.

rubrics_metrics.name: CharacterTableRegular purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: CharacterTableRegular(tbl,p) returns the 'table head' of the p-modular Brauer character table of tbl: the restriction of tbl to its p-regular classes, but without irreducible Brauer characters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This returned table head can be used to create p-modular Brauer characters by restricting ordinary characters, useful when irreducible Brauer characters are hard to compute or BrauerTable(tbl,p) returns fail. Examples show equality checks among CharacterTable(tbl,2), BrauerTable(tbl,2), etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: SupportedCharacterTableInfo purpose in conversions
rubrics_metrics.description: SupportedCharacterTableInfo is a list specifying which record components (when converting a record to a character table) should be treated as attribute values, and which of character/class/mutable they depend on.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When converting records to character tables via ConvertToCharacterTable, only components named in SupportedCharacterTableInfo are interpreted as attribute values; others become simple components. New attributes/properties intended for conversion must be created with DeclareAttributeSuppCT / DeclarePropertySuppCT rather than the standard DeclareAttribute / DeclareProperty.

rubrics_metrics.name: ConvertToCharacterTable and NC variant
rubrics_metrics.description: ConvertToCharacterTable(record) converts a record into a character table component object, using SupportedCharacterTableInfo to map record components to attributes; ConvertToCharacterTableNC does the same but omits all checks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If inconsistencies in record are detected, ConvertToCharacterTable returns fail. The record must have UnderlyingCharacteristic bound, because that decides whether the returned table is IsOrdinaryTable or IsBrauerTable. For examples see PrintCharacterTable (71.13.5).

rubrics_metrics.name: Character table categories and their meanings
rubrics_metrics.description: Every character-table-like object lies in IsNearlyCharacterTable. Important subcategories: IsOrdinaryTable (ordinary tables), IsBrauerTable (Brauer tables), IsCharacterTable (union of ordinary and Brauer), and IsCharacterTableInProgress (incomplete ordinary tables).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IsOrdinaryTable/IsBrauerTable denote tables that provide enough info to compute all power maps and irreducible characters (e.g., underlying group known or library table). Objects in IsCharacterTable are immutable (ordering of conjugacy classes fixed). IsCharacterTableInProgress objects are mutable and represent incomplete ordinary tables (not all irreducibles, power maps, or even class counts may be known); such tables may contain unknowns or lists of possible values for some attributes and are currently not fully supported; a table with access to its group is always complete even if Irr not stored.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conventions for character-table ordering and defaults
rubrics_metrics.description: Conventions: the class of the identity element is expected to be the first class; the trivial character need not be the first in the list of irreducibles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Most functions that take a character table expect characters as arguments; in some functions the list of irreducible characters (Irr) serves as default and Irr will be computed automatically if not yet known. For a stored class fusion, the image table is denoted by its Identifier value; each library table has a unique identifier, and constructed tables get a session-unique identifier.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interface between character tables and groups (three required attributes)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a character table with an underlying group, the interface between table and group consists of three attribute values: the group (UnderlyingGroup), the conjugacy classes stored in the table (ConjugacyClasses), and the identification of the conjugacy classes of table and group (IdentificationOfConjugacyClasses).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Character tables constructed from groups know these values upon construction. Tasks may be delegated between a group and its character table only if these three attribute values are stored in the character table. CharacterTableWithStoredGroup tries to set these consistently when connecting a group with a library table.

rubrics_metrics.name: UnderlyingGroup attribute semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: For an ordinary character table ordtbl of a finite group, the group can be stored as the value of UnderlyingGroup; Brauer tables do not store the underlying group and access it via the ordinary table.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Storing UnderlyingGroup allows delegation of computations between the table and the group; Brauer tables rely on their ordinary table for access to the group.

rubrics_metrics.name: ConjugacyClasses attribute semantics and ordering caveat
rubrics_metrics.description: ConjugacyClasses(tbl) for a character table tbl with known underlying group G returns a list of conjugacy classes of G; attributes related to ordering (centralizer sizes, orders of representatives, power maps, class functions) refer to this ordering.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This ordering need not coincide with the ordering of conjugacy classes stored in the underlying group (to allow use of library tables as character tables of groups with pre-stored class info). The identity class must be first. If tbl was constructed from G the classes are stored; there is no method that computes ConjugacyClasses for tbl if not stored. Brauer tables do not store p-regular conjugacy classes directly but access them via the ordinary table.

rubrics_metrics.name: IdentificationOfConjugacyClasses mapping
rubrics_metrics.description: IdentificationOfConjugacyClasses(tbl) returns a list l where l[i] is the position of the i-th conjugacy class of tbl in the ConjugacyClasses value of the underlying group (when known).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This attribute describes how columns of the table map to the group's stored conjugacy class list. Example usage: after setting ConjugacyClasses in a group and calling CharacterTable, IdentificationOfConjugacyClasses shows the mapping such as [5,1,2,3,4].

rubrics_metrics.name: CharacterTableWithStoredGroup matching rules
rubrics_metrics.description: CharacterTableWithStoredGroup(G, tbl[, info]) tries to identify the classes of a group G with the columns of a character table tbl via CompatibleConjugacyClasses and, if identification is unique up to automorphisms of tbl, stores tbl as the CharacterTable value of G and returns a new table equivalent to tbl with UnderlyingGroup, ConjugacyClasses, and IdentificationOfConjugacyClasses set.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If GAP cannot identify the classes up to automorphisms of tbl then fail is returned. If an info record is provided it is passed to CompatibleConjugacyClasses as arec. If a list is given as third argument it is used directly as IdentificationOfConjugacyClasses (without checking). Typical call sequence: first use CompatibleConjugacyClasses(tbl) to check feasibility, then CharacterTableWithStoredGroup when unique identification is likely.

rubrics_metrics.name: CompatibleConjugacyClasses invariants and options
rubrics_metrics.description: CompatibleConjugacyClasses([G,ccl,]tbl[,arec]) checks whether columns of tbl can be identified with conjugacy classes ccl of group G (or for a group isomorphic to the one tbl represents) and returns a list describing identifications that are unique up to automorphisms of tbl; if identification is ambiguous it returns lists of indistinguishable class-position sets or fail if no identification is possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Invariants used for identification: (1) element orders (OrdersClassRepresentatives), (2) class lengths (SizesConjugacyClasses), (3) power maps (PowerMap, ComputedPowerMaps), (4) symmetries of the table (AutomorphismsOfTable). The optional arec record may supply 'natchar' (natural character values if G is a permutation or matrix group) and 'bijection' (partial bijection where i-th entry, if bound, gives position of i-th class of tbl in ccl). Typical approach: call the second form (tbl only) to test quickly before doing the more expensive G + ccl computation. Example: CompatibleConjugacyClasses( CharacterTable( "J2" ) ) may return ambiguous sets like [ [17,18], [9,10] ].
